help.title: User Manual
help.subtitle: Complete guide to using the Seedling Desktop application.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.content:
### Logging In

1. Open the Seedling Desktop app in your web browser.
2. On the login screen, select your name from the dropdown list.
3. Enter your 4-digit PIN (your Employee Number).
4. Click Sign In.

If your PIN is incorrect, an error message will appear. Contact an administrator if you need your PIN reset.

### First-Time Users

Your administrator must create your employee account in the Employees reference table before you can log in. You will need:

- Your name added to the system
- A 4-digit Employee Number assigned (this is your PIN)
- An appropriate User Level assigned

### User Roles

- Level 1 (User) — View all data, no editing
- Level 2 (Breeder) — Add/edit crosses, inline editing of shipping and comments
- Level 3 (Admin2) — Manage Teams, Trays, Ratios, Deadlines, and Employees
- Level 4 (Admin3) — Same as Admin2
- Level 5 (Molecular) — Manage Labs, Markers, Marker Allocations, and Marker Prices

navigation.title: Navigation & Layout
navigation.content:
The app uses a sidebar on the left side of the screen for navigation. It is organized into four sections:

- Home & Analytics — Dashboard overview and detailed charts
- Crosses — Cross records, parent inventory, and the cross form
- Propagation Lifecycle — Stage-by-stage tracking from pollen through shipping
- Reference Tables — System configuration data (teams, labs, markers, etc.)

### Sidebar Controls

- Click the pin icon to keep the sidebar always visible, or let it collapse automatically.
- Click your user avatar at the bottom to log out.
- Right-click a section icon when collapsed to see the flyout menu.

The top bar contains the global filters that apply across all pages.

globalFilters.title: Global Filters
globalFilters.content:
The top bar contains persistent filters that affect data across every page:

- Berry Type — Filter by berry (e.g., Strawberry, Blueberry, Raspberry, Blackberry)
- Team — Filter by breeding team
- Pollination Year — Select the target pollination year
- SP Crosses — Toggle to show/hide SP (specific) crosses

These filters stay active as you navigate between pages. To see all data, clear any active filters.

dashboard.title: Home Dashboard
dashboard.content:
The dashboard provides a quick overview of the current breeding season's progress.

### Progress Cards

Four color-coded progress cards at the top show:

- Pollination Progress — Percentage of pollinations completed vs. required
- Seed Progress — Seed collected (grams) vs. required
- Transplant Progress — Seedlings transplanted vs. required
- Ship Progress — Seedlings shipped vs. total requested

Each card shows a progress bar that shifts from red (behind schedule) to green (on track).

### Charts

- Crosses by Berry Type — Bar chart showing active crosses for each berry type
- Propagation Funnel — Funnel chart visualizing volume through stages: Ship Request, Transplants Required, Pollinations Required, Crosses

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.content:
The Analytics page provides detailed charts and breakdowns beyond the dashboard summary.

- Pollinations, Seed, Transplants, and Shipping — Grouped bar charts filterable by Program, Destination, Team, or Year
- Marker Analytics — Compares Marker Totals (Allocated vs. Cross List vs. Actual) and shows Markers Planned by Type
- Parent Analytics — Charts for female and male parent performance including Seed Weight and Fruit Percentage

Use the dropdown controls on the page to switch between different chart groupings.

crosses.title: Crosses
crosses.content: The Crosses section manages all cross records, parent plant inventory, and the form for creating or editing crosses.

simplified.title: Crossing List (Simplified)
simplified.content:
A condensed table showing the most commonly referenced cross data.

### Key Columns

- Progeny name, Destination 1 & 2, Ship Requests, Adjustments
- Total Ship Requirement, Estimated Plants to Ship, Est Ship # (from Seed)
- Transplant progress (Done vs. Required), Extra Trays Available
- Markers, Seed data, Parent counts, Plant Date

### Color Coding

- Est Ship # (from Seed): Green if meeting/exceeding the Total Ship Requirement; red if falling short
- D1/D2 Adj +/-: Amber highlight when adjustments have been entered

### Actions

- Add Cross button (Breeder level and above)
- Full List button to switch to the comprehensive view
- Row actions: Edit, Copy as New, Inactivate

### Inline Editing (Breeder level and above)

- Destination 1 & 2, Adjustments, Expected Discard %, Spiny Discard %

full.title: Crossing List (Full)
full.content:
The comprehensive table showing all cross data fields. This view contains all columns from the Simplified list, plus:

- Parent 1 & 2 names, Berry type, Team
- Screening status and Marker 1–6 assignments, Lab 1–2
- Seed details (Sow Seed?, Seed Sown, Seed Weight Required/Inventory)
- Fruit and Flower data (Required vs. Collected/Pollinated)
- Parent layer details (P1/P2 L1–L4 field codes and counts)
- Reciprocal Done, Fumigated, SP Crosses, Breeder & GH Team Comments

### Inline Editing (Breeder level and above)

- Destination 1 & 2, D1/D2 Adjustments, Expected Discard %, Spiny Discard %
- Breeder Comments, GH Team Comments

### Batch Save

After making inline edits across multiple rows, click Save to submit all changes at once.

form.title: Cross Form (Add / Edit / Copy)
form.content:
The form for creating a new cross, editing an existing one, or copying a cross to create a new record.

### Sections

- Cross Info: Berry, Progeny, Pollination Year/Team, Parents (searchable dropdowns), Reciprocal, SP Crosses, Designed By
- Destinations & Shipping: Location, Program, Ship Request, Ship Adjustment, Field Plant Date — for Destination 1 and 2
- Screening & Markers: Screening toggle, Marker 1–6 (filtered by berry type), Lab 1–2
- Calculations Panel: Read-only panel showing calculated propagation requirements

### Modes

- Add: All fields editable. A new cross is created on save.
- Edit: Some fields locked (Berry, Progeny, Year/Team, Ship Request). Other fields can be updated.
- Copy as New: Data pre-filled from existing cross; you must enter a new Progeny name.

parents.title: Parent Inventory
parents.content:
Manages parent plant inventory used in crosses.

### Columns

- Selection name (the parent variety)
- L1 Field Code & L1 Count (primary location)
- L2–L4 Field Codes & Counts (toggleable with Show/Hide L2–L4 button)
- Total Parents, Parents Required, Year, Comments, Berry, Team

### Row Highlighting

- Rows highlighted in red if the parent does not have sufficient plants to meet requirements

### Actions

- Add Parent — Create a new parent record with location and count details
- Edit — Update an existing parent's locations and inventory
- Delete — Remove a parent record

propagation.title: Propagation Lifecycle
propagation.content: The Propagation Lifecycle pages track the progress of crosses through each stage of the breeding process, from pollen collection to final shipping.

lifecycle.title: Lifecycle Summary
lifecycle.content:
A high-level checklist showing the completion status of each lifecycle stage.

- Stages tracked: Pollen, Pollination, Fruit, Seed, Transplant, Screen, Ship
- Administrators can toggle the Done status for any stage
- Shows who last modified the status and when

pollen.title: Pollen
pollen.content:
Tracks flower collection and pollen availability for each parent plant.

- Flowers Required for Pollen vs. Total Flowers Collected
- Pollen Available, Pollen Used, Bad Pollen
- L1–L4 Field Codes and collection counts (L2–L4 toggleable)
- Pollen To Go filter highlights parents that still need more flowers collected
- Totals row displays sum totals for key numeric columns

pollination.title: Pollination
pollination.content:
Monitors the execution of crosses between parent plants.

- Progeny, Parent 1, Parent 2, Bulk Parent 3
- Pollination Required vs. Successful Pollinations, Emasculation To Go
- Reciprocal Done status
- Label Export feature for printing field labels (CSV)

fruit.title: Fruit
fruit.content:
Tracks fruit collection progress after successful pollinations.

- Progeny, Fruit Required, Total Fruit Collected
- Fruit To Go filter highlights crosses where the collection target has not been met

seed.title: Seed
seed.content:
Manages seed processing, including acid treatment and sowing.

- Seed Weight Required, Seed Weight Inventory
- Seed Ready for Acid/GA treatment status
- Seed Weight to Sow vs. Seed Weight to Bank (storage)
- Acid/GA treatment start dates and deadlines, Sow Start date
- Treatment Tracking automatically flags seeds ready for processing
- Calculations Panel explains the logic behind seed sowing and banking

transplant.title: Transplant
transplant.content:
Tracks the transplanting of germinated seedlings into trays.

- Transplants Required vs. Plants Transplanted
- Transplant Instructions (e.g., Al Azar, Spineless, Spiny)
- Destination 1 & 2 quantities
- Breeders can modify D1/D2 transplant adjustments

screenProgeny.title: Screening (by Progeny)
screenProgeny.content:
Shows genotype screening status summarized by cross/progeny.

- Progeny, Markers assigned, Samples Required vs. Collected
- Keep Requests vs. Keep Actuals
- Sort Groups (1–5) for organizing screening results

screenPlate.title: Screening (by Plate)
screenPlate.content:
Shows genotype screening status organized by physical lab plates.

- Plate Index, Lab, Marker
- Samples Required vs. Collected
- Screening completion status

sortAllocation.title: Sort Group Allocation
sortAllocation.content:
Used between screening and shipping to split each progeny's screened-and-kept Sort Group counts (1–5) between its two destinations (D1 and D2).

Requires Berry, Team, and Pollination Year set in the top filters. Only progenies with both D1 and D2 destinations and at least one non-zero Sort Group appear.

For each Sort Group, pick a priority:
- Equal split — divide 50/50, capped by each side's ship request.
- D1 priority — fill D1 up to its ship request, overflow to D2.
- D2 priority — mirror of D1.

Priorities apply from SG1 → SG5 in order, tracking remaining ship-request capacity per side. The D1 + D2 split always equals the source Sort Group total.

Save All writes every progeny's split in one transaction. Save is rejected if any (progeny, sort group) exceeds the source total. Breeder (level 2) or higher can save.

ship.title: Ship
ship.content:
The final stage — preparing and tracking seedling shipments.

- Progeny, Destination, Total Ship Plan vs. Ship Actual Total
- First Tray/Box, Last Tray/Box, Rack/Pallet information
- Extras Not Shipped (seedlings exceeding requirements)

reference.title: Reference Tables
reference.content: Reference tables contain the configuration data that drives calculations and options throughout the app. These are typically managed by administrators.

labs.title: Labs
labs.content:
Manage the external testing laboratories used for genotype screening.

- Lab Name — Name of the testing lab
- Plate Sample Number — Standard capacity of a plate at this lab
- Active — Whether the lab is currently available for selection

Only Molecular (Level 5) users can create, edit, or inactivate labs. All other users have read-only access.

teams.title: Teams
teams.content:
Manage the breeding teams within the organization.

- Team Name — Name of the team
- Active — Whether the team is currently active

Only Admin2 (Level 3) and Admin3 (Level 4) users can create, edit, or inactivate teams. All other users have read-only access.

trays.title: Trays
trays.content:
Define the standard tray sizes used in the greenhouse.

- Tray Size — Number of cells in the tray
- M² Per Tray — Surface area of the tray

Only Admin2 (Level 3) and Admin3 (Level 4) users can create, edit, or inactivate trays. All other users have read-only access.

ratios.title: Ratios
ratios.content:
Manage success percentages and yield factors used in propagation calculations.

- Seedling Transplant Success %, Average Seed Germination %, Pollination Success %
- Seeds Per Gram, Grams of Seed Per Fruit
- Standard Deviations for germination, pollination, and flower collection
- Each ratio is linked to a specific Team, Berry, and Program

Only Admin2 (Level 3) and Admin3 (Level 4) users can create, edit, or inactivate ratios. All other users have read-only access.

deadlines.title: Deadlines
deadlines.content:
Configure the operational schedule for each stage of the breeding lifecycle.

- Milestones: Crossing Files, Pollination, Fruit Collection, Seed Treatment, Sowing, Transplanting, Marker Screening
- Each milestone has a Start Week and Deadline Week (relative to a target date)
- Deadlines can be set per Berry Type, Team, Destination, and Program
- Drives notifications that alert team members when action items are approaching

Only Admin2 (Level 3) and Admin3 (Level 4) users can create, edit, or inactivate deadlines. All other users have read-only access.

employees.title: Employees
employees.content:
Manage user accounts and access permissions.

- Employee Name — Full name displayed in the system
- Employee Number — 4-digit code used as the login PIN (hidden for non-admin users)
- Team — Assigned breeding team
- Email — Used for automated notifications
- User Level — Permission level (User, Breeder, Admin2, Admin3, Molecular)
- Active — Whether the account is enabled

All users can view the Employees screen, but only Admin2 (Level 3) and Admin3 (Level 4) can create, edit, or inactivate employees. Employee numbers are masked with dots for non-admin users.

markers.title: Marker List
markers.content:
Manage the catalog of genetic markers (traits) available for screening.

- Trait/Marker Name, Berry type, Preferred Lab
- Aliases (Driscoll's or Corteva names)
- Lab Status for each lab (e.g., Corteva, LGC)

Only Molecular (Level 5) users can create, edit, or inactivate markers. Berry, Preferred Lab, and Alias (Driscolls) are required fields. All other users have read-only access.

markerBudget.title: Marker Allocations / Budget
markerBudget.content:
Track the budget and sample limits for genotyping activities.

- Sample Allocation Total — Maximum number of samples allowed
- Cost Allocation Total — Budget amount for genotyping
- Linked to Pollination Year, Berry, Program, Lab, and Team

Only Molecular (Level 5) users can add, edit, or delete marker allocations. All other users have read-only access.

markerPrices.title: Marker Prices
markerPrices.content:
Manage the unit costs for genetic testing services.

- Sample Price — Cost per sample
- Year, Berry, Genotyping Screen, Lab

Only Molecular (Level 5) users can add, edit, or delete marker prices. All other users have read-only access.

languages.title: Language Support
languages.content:
The app supports four languages:

- English
- Spanish (Español)
- Portuguese (Português)
- Arabic (العربية) — displayed in right-to-left layout

To change the language, use the language selector in the top bar. The entire interface will update to your selected language.

roles.title: User Roles & Permissions
roles.content:
Access to features is controlled by your assigned User Level:

- Level 1 (User) — View all data across the app. No editing capabilities. Employee numbers are hidden.
- Level 2 (Breeder) — Add/edit crosses, inline edit shipping adjustments, comments, and discard percentages. Employee numbers are hidden.
- Level 3 (Admin2) — All Breeder capabilities, plus manage Teams, Trays, Ratios, Deadlines, and Employees. Toggle lifecycle stage completion.
- Level 4 (Admin3) — All Admin2 capabilities.
- Level 5 (Molecular) — Manage Labs, Marker List, Marker Allocations, and Marker Prices. Read-only access to Teams, Trays, Ratios, Deadlines, and Employees. Employee numbers are hidden.

### Screen Access Summary

- Teams, Trays, Ratios, Deadlines, Employees — Editable by Admin2 (Level 3) and Admin3 (Level 4) only. All other users have read-only access.
- Labs, Marker List, Marker Allocations, Marker Prices — Editable by Molecular (Level 5) only. All other users have read-only access.
- Employees screen — Visible to all users, but Employee Numbers are masked (shown as dots) for non-admin users.

Your User Level is assigned by an administrator in the Employees reference table.

tips.title: Tips & Shortcuts
tips.content:
- Inline Editing: On the Crossing Lists, click directly into editable cells to make quick changes. Click Save to submit your batch.
- Batch Save: All changes are saved together — no need to save each row individually.
- Sticky Headers: Table headers stay visible as you scroll down.
- Color Coding: Green on Est Ship # (from Seed) means meeting the requirement; red means falling short. Amber on adjustment columns indicates an adjustment. Red rows in Parent Inventory mean insufficient parents.
- Copy as New: Use this action on any cross to quickly create a similar cross with a new Progeny name.
- Pollen/Fruit To Go: Use these filters to focus on items that still need attention.
- Label Export: On the Pollination page, export CSV files for printing field labels.
- Reset Filters: Every gallery page has a Reset button to clear all filters.
